identity.why: The pinned upstream commit still carries the three delivery defects. The running artifact is a built wheel carrying the reviewed repair, so the certified identity is that wheel's sha256 plus version, not a commit it does not have. Asking a wheel for a commit can only ever produce a permanent false red, which teaches people to ignore the gate.
identity.retired_when: the repair lands upstream and a release is installed from source, then identity.accepted returns to upstream_pin

deployed_build.identity: local reviewed wheel, not the pinned upstream release commit
deployed_build.why: The three known blockers are reproduced defects of the pinned release. The running artifact carries a reviewed source repair, so it has its own identity rather than borrowing the upstream commit.
not_verified: real Gateway model turn, follow-up and final reply on this exact build
restart and crash recovery with an in-flight turn
topic reply, clarify, approval and media round trips
two consecutive long turns and a queued follow-up
deployed_build.owner_note: Automated contracts passing is not interaction acceptance. The upstream pin stays quarantined; this record only identifies what is actually running.

compatibility_exception.why: This fixed candidate supports all delivery anchors; only optional context-compaction status visibility is unavailable. Tool and answer updates remain supported. Full compatibility remains separately reported.
